sources.title: Sakana Namazu API release
sources.evidence: August3,2026 announcement explicitly releases an updated Japanese-focused Kimi K2.6 adaptation through the API. It distinguishes earlier Chat versions and describes additional training, image understanding and function calling.

sources.title: Sakana Namazu product and FAQ
sources.evidence: Product FAQ explicitly says Sakana starts from open Kimi K2.6 and applies additional training for Japanese performance and neutral responses. It offers hosted API access, not Namazu checkpoint files.

sources.title: Exact Namazu model and API documentation
sources.evidence: Binds sakana-namazu to sakana-namazu-v1.0; specifies256K context, text/image input, text responses, extended thinking with on/off controls, model-selected function tools and autonomous built-in web search/code execution. Document files are processed through API/tool facilities.

sources.title: Pinned Kimi K2.6 base-model card
sources.evidence: The explicitly named base is MoE with nominal1T total and32B activated parameters; card describes MoonViT separately. These numeric counts are for Kimi K2.6, not a direct Namazu disclosure.

sources.title: Pinned Kimi K2.6 configuration
sources.evidence: KimiK25ForConditionalGeneration contains kimi_k2 text configuration with61layers,384routed experts and8 selected experts. Confirms the named base architecture; this is not a published Namazu configuration.

sources.title: Namazu alpha prototypes and Sakana Chat launch
sources.evidence: March24,2026 launches a prototype series: Namazu-DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus, Llama-3.1-Namazu-405B and Namazu-gpt-oss-120B. These distinct bases do not date or size the later Kimi K2.6 API model.

sources.title: Sakana Chat adds Fugu and a new Namazu generation
sources.evidence: August13,2026 updates Chat to the new Namazu generation and links its already-available API. Image/document attachments and Python execution are application capabilities; no model parameter count is supplied.

sources.title: Sakana Translate adopts new-generation Namazu
sources.evidence: August21,2026 identifies the model as the generation recently released through API and Chat, with refreshed base and improved posttraining. Translation comparisons provide no exact Namazu total/active count or neural configuration.

sources.title: Namazu adoption in Evidence Finder
sources.evidence: October9,2026 discusses the current model’s posttraining and Japanese capabilities, preserving base reasoning/knowledge/coding. It gives application benchmarks but no exact parameter total, active convention or structural change.

sources.title: Sakana API platform terms
sources.evidence: Service/configuration rights remain with Sakana and relevant licensors, with permission limited to service use. This supports Proprietary hosted-model classification; the base model’s license does not grant access to Namazu weights.

sources.title: Exact Sakana-hosted Namazu endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: The Sakana AI endpoint advertises context_length262144 and max_completion_tokens65536. Text/image/file input and text output are listed. Its August11 provider identifier/listing is not the August3 original API release.

sources.title: Official SakanaAI model inventory
sources.evidence: All49 returned official models were inspected; none is a Namazu checkpoint. The67-repository public GitHub organization inventory also contains no Namazu-named repository. No exact public weights or neural configuration were located.

sources.title: Sakana research and product archive
sources.evidence: Reviewed Namazu launch, alpha and later Chat/Translate/medical updates, and separate sparsity/recursive-improvement research. MayTwELL concerns experimental sparse models; OctoberMASS uses Qwen3.6-27B. Neither binds its architecture/count to Namazu.

name.note: Exact hosted API product, currently identified as sakana-namazu-v1.0; not a combined count of the March alpha prototypes.

developer.note: Sakana performs the Japanese adaptation; Moonshot AI develops the named Kimi K2.6 base.

family.note: Normalized Namazu product lineage. The family contains different base-model generations; family membership does not imply identical architecture or size.

release_date.note: Explicit release of the updated Kimi K2.6-based API model. March24 dates other alpha prototypes; August13 and21 are subsequent Chat/Translate rollouts, not the first API release.

open_weights.note: Distributed as restricted hosted API access. The base is open-weight, but no public Namazu checkpoint was identified in official inventories.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-model classification. Do not transfer Kimi K2.6’s Modified MIT license to unpublished Namazu weights or confuse service access with weight redistribution.

parameters_b.note: Exact Namazu total is undisclosed in the checked primary sources. The named Kimi K2.6 base has nominal1T, but no Namazu count or explicit unchanged-parameter-structure statement permits copying it into this field. No own checkpoint enables reconstruction.

active_parameters_b.note: No Namazu-specific active count or counting convention is published. Kimi K2.6’s nominal32B activated figure is base-model evidence only; it is not transferred to the derivative.

architecture.note: Lineage-based inference: Sakana explicitly starts from Kimi K2.6 and applies additional training, while the pinned base card/config verify a neural MoE Transformer. This establishes the broad MoE classification, not a claim that every dimension, parameter or vision component is unchanged. No Namazu configuration is public.

context_window.note: Advertised hosted capacity: developer documents256K and the exact Sakana AI endpoint gives262144 tokens. This is a serving limit, not an independently verified native training maximum; endpoint completion cap is65536.

modalities.note: Developer documents image inputs and text responses. PDF/Office/CSV files are API containers handled through tool facilities, not separate neural modalities. No video capability is inherited from Kimi K2.6.

reasoning.note: Extended thinking is explicitly documented and enabled by default, with enable/disable controls and reasoning output. No unsupported effort levels are inferred from generic provider metadata.

tool_call.note: The model selects caller-defined functions and built-in web_search/code_interpreter tools; documentation explicitly describes autonomous tool loops. Tool execution can generate files without making media generation a neural output modality.

description.value: Japanese-language adaptation of Kimi K2.6, trained for Japanese language and business contexts with thinking and tool use.
description.note: Describes documented lineage, specialization and capabilities without unsupported benchmark-superiority claims.

patch.description: Japanese-language adaptation of Kimi K2.6, trained for Japanese language and business contexts with thinking and tool use.
patch.notes: This record describes the Kimi K2.6-based Sakana Namazu API released August 3, 2026, currently sakana-namazu-v1.0. March alpha prototypes used different bases. MoE is inferred from Sakana’s explicit additional-training lineage and the official Kimi K2.6 architecture; exact Namazu total/active counts remain undisclosed. Base-model nominal 1T/32B figures are not asserted as Namazu counts. The 262,144-token context is the advertised Sakana-hosted endpoint limit. File attachments are API/tool facilities; neural modalities are text/image input and text output. No authenticated inference request was made.

summary: Verified August3 Kimi K2.6-based API release, currentv1.0 identity, advertised context, thinking and tools. Added Proprietary and broad MoE classification from explicit fine-tuning lineage, with inference clearly qualified; removed PDF as a separate neural modality. Exact derivative parameter counts remain undisclosed after later product/research/comparison and public-inventory checks. March alpha prototypes are distinct.
